1.title: Requests, Limits, Quotas and LimitRange
1.text: Welcome to Module ten: Requests, Limits, Quotas and Limit Range. It covers the exam area Application Environment, Configuration and Security. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, and every task was run on a real cluster, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do three things. Understand requests, limits, quotas. Define resource requirements. Practice with six hands-on labs worth thirty-eight points.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Application Environment, Configuration and Security (twenty-five percent). Practice in this module: six labs, thirty-eight points, about thirty-nine minutes. Exam format: performance-based tasks in a live terminal, scored on the final cluster state. Validated on: Kubernetes version one point thirty-seven point zero.

1.title: Requests and limits
1.text: Requests and limits. The figure shows this: Requests are for scheduling, limits are enforced at run time. Exam tip: Requests decide where a Pod is scheduled; a container above its memory limit is O O M killed, above its C P U limit it is throttled.

1.title: Requests and limits, continued
1.text: Requests and limits. Every container can declare how much C P U and memory it needs. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: Requests and limits, continued
1.text: Requests and limits. Who uses it. Request: the scheduler: a Pod goes only to a node with enough unreserved capacity. Limit: the kubelet and the container runtime. C P U over the value. Request: n or a. Limit: the container is throttled (slowed), not killed. Memory over the value. Request: n or a. Limit: the container is killed ( O O M killed, exit code one hundred thirty-seven) and restarted. If missing. Request: treated as zero (or the Limit Range default). Limit: no limit (or the Limit Range default); if only a limit is set, the request equals it.

1.title: Requests and limits, continued
1.text: Requests and limits. Units. C P U: one is one core, five hundred millicores is half a core (milli-C P U). Memory: bytes with suffixes Ki, Mi, Gi (powers of one thousand twenty-four) or K, M, G (powers of one thousand). one hundred twenty-eight mebibytes and one hundred twenty-eight megabytes are different. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: Requests and limits, continued
1.text: Requests and limits. A Pod whose requests do not fit on any node stays Pending with "zero or three nodes are available:... Insufficient cpu". Fix it by lowering the request (a bare Pod must be recreated; a Deployment is edited) or by freeing capacity.

1.title: Quality of Service classes
1.text: Quality of Service classes. Kubernetes puts each Pod into a Qo S class from its requests and limits. The class decides who is evicted first when a node runs out of memory. Guaranteed. Rule: every container has requests equal to limits for both C P U and memory. Eviction order: last. Burstable. Rule: at least one request or limit set, but not Guaranteed. Eviction order: middle. Best Effort. Rule: no requests and no limits at all. Eviction order: first. Read it with kube control get pod pod dash o json path dot status dot qos Class. Exam tip: A Pod is Guaranteed only when every container has requests equal to its limits.

1.title: ResourceQuota: a budget per namespace
1.text: Resource Quota: a budget per namespace. A Resource Quota caps what a whole namespace may use. It is how an administrator shares a cluster between teams. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study. Exam tip: Read the quota with kube control describe quota; a full quota stops the Replica Set from creating Pods.

1.title: ResourceQuota: a budget per namespace, continued
1.text: Resource Quota: a budget per namespace. pods, services, configmaps, secrets, persistentvolumeclaims. the count of objects. requests dot cpu, requests dot memory. the sum of requests of all Pods. limits dot cpu, limits dot memory. the sum of limits of all Pods. requests dot storage. the sum of P V C (Persistent Volume Claim) sizes. Two consequences you must know. When a quota covers C P U or memory ( requests. or limits. ), every new Pod must declare that request or limit, or the A P I server rejects it: must specify limits dot memory. Add the values, or create a Limit Range that supplies defaults.

1.title: ResourceQuota: a budget per namespace, continued
1.text: Resource Quota: a budget per namespace. When a quota is full, the Deployment is accepted but its Replica Set cannot create the Pods: get deploy shows two slash four, and the cause is in kube control get events or kube control describe rs: forbidden exceeded quota. Raise the quota or lower the usage.

1.title: LimitRange: defaults and bounds per container
1.text: Limit Range: defaults and bounds per container. A Limit Range works inside a namespace on each container or Pod: it fills in defaults and rejects values outside min and max. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study. Exam tip: A Limit Range fills in defaults for new Pods only and rejects values above its maximum.

1.title: LimitRange: defaults and bounds per container, continued
1.text: Limit Range: defaults and bounds per container. The defaults apply when a Pod is created: existing Pods are not changed. A Pod that asks for more than max is rejected with maximum cpu usage per Container is five hundred millicores, but limit is one. Quotas and Limit Ranges are checked by admission control when the object is created (Module eleven), not while the Pod runs. Scope. Resource Quota: the whole namespace (sum). Limit Range: one container, Pod or P V C. Does. Resource Quota: caps totals and counts. Limit Range: sets defaults, min and max. Needs the Pod to declare resources. Resource Quota: yes (for the covered resources). Limit Range: no: it can supply them.

1.title: When the limit is hit
1.text: When the limit is hit. O O M killed, exit code one hundred thirty-seven, restarts. Meaning: memory use above the limit. Fix: raise the memory limit (and request) or fix the leak. App slow, C P U at its limit in kube control top. Meaning: C P U throttling. Fix: raise the C P U limit. Pending, Insufficient cpu slash memory. Meaning: the request does not fit any node. Fix: lower the request. forbidden exceeded quota. Meaning: the namespace budget is spent. Fix: raise the quota or remove objects. must specify limits dot memory. Meaning: quota requires it. Fix: add resources or a Limit Range default.

1.title: When the limit is hit, continued
1.text: When the limit is hit. Exam tip. In "set the resources of this Deployment" tasks use kube control set resources deployment name the requests flag set to... the limits flag set to...: one command, and it triggers the rollout for you. Exam tip. kube control describe quota shows Used and Hard: read it before you change anything. Do not delete a quota to "fix" a task unless the task says so.

1.title: Lab 10.1: requests limits qos
1.text: Lab ten point one: requests limits qos. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. In the namespace res, create a Pod named sized (image engine X alpine ) whose container requests one hundred millicores C P U and sixty-four mebibytes memory and is limited to two hundred millicores C P U and one hundred twenty-eight mebibytes memory. Wait until it is Running. Then write the Pod's Qo S class (just the class name) to about slash answers slash qos dot txt on the host where you run kube control. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

1.title: Lab 10.1: requests limits qos, Solution
1.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n res run sized the image flag set to engine X alpine the dry run flag set to client dash o yaml slash temp slash sized dot yaml. Then make the edit with sed, as shown on the screen. Then kube control apply dash f slash temp slash sized dot yaml. Then kube control dash n res wait the for flag set to condition Ready pod slash sized the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then kube control dash n res get pod sized dash o json path dot status dot qos Class about slash answers slash qos dot txt. Then cat about slash answers slash qos dot txt. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

1.title: Lab 10.2: oomkilled limit
1.text: Lab ten point two: oomkilled limit. This task is worth seven points, and you should plan about eight minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. In the namespace res, the Pod of the Deployment hog is repeatedly killed because it uses more memory than its limit ( O O M killed ). Without changing the image or the command, set the memory limit of its container to two hundred fifty-six mebibytes and its memory request to sixty-four mebibytes, and wait until the Deployment has one Ready replica that keeps running. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 10.2: oomkilled limit, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n res describe pod dash l app hog then pipe to grep -i E O O M killed then pipe to Reason then pipe to Limits then pipe to memory. Then kube control dash n res set resources deployment hog the requests flag set to memory sixty-four mebibytes the limits flag set to memory two hundred fifty-six mebibytes. Then kube control dash n res rollout status deployment hog the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 10.3: resource quota
2.text: Lab ten point three: resource quota. This task is worth seven points, and you should plan about seven minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. In the namespace quota, create a Resource Quota named team quota that allows at most three Pods, five hundred millicores of total C P U requests and one gibibyte of total memory limits. Then create a Deployment web (image engine X alpine, two replicas) whose Pods each request one hundred millicores C P U and have a memory limit of two hundred fifty-six mebibytes, so that both replicas are Ready within the quota. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 10.3: resource quota, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n quota create quota team quota the hard flag set to pods three,requests dot cpu five hundred millicores,limits dot memory one gibibyte. Then kube control dash n quota create deployment web the image flag set to engine X alpine the replicas flag set to two the dry run flag set to client dash o yaml slash temp, and so on. Then make the edit with sed, as shown on the screen. Then kube control apply dash f slash temp slash web dot yaml. Then kube control dash n quota rollout status deployment web the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then kube control dash n quota describe quota team quota. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 10.4: quota exceeded
2.text: Lab ten point four: quota exceeded. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. In the namespace quota, the Deployment batch should run four replicas, but only two Pods exist: the events show that the Pods exceed the Resource Quota limits pods. Do not change the Deployment: raise the quota so that it allows four Pods, and wait until all four replicas are Ready. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 10.4: quota exceeded, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n quota describe quota limits pods. Then kube control dash n quota get events the sort by flag set to dot last Timestamp then pipe to tail -three. Then kube control dash n quota patch quota limits pods dash p spec hard pods four. Then kube control dash n quota rollout status deployment batch the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 10.5: limitrange defaults
2.text: Lab ten point five: limitrange defaults. This task is worth seven points, and you should plan about seven minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. In the namespace lr, create a Limit Range named defaults for containers: default limits two hundred millicores C P U and one hundred twenty-eight mebibytes memory, default requests one hundred millicores C P U and sixty-four mebibytes memory, and a maximum of five hundred millicores C P U per container. Then create a Pod plain (image engine X alpine ) without any resources, and confirm that it received the defaults. A Pod that asks for one C P U must be rejected in this namespace. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 10.5: limitrange defaults, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. kube control dash n lr apply dash f -. The manifest comes next, as shown on the screen. Then kube control dash n lr run plain the image flag set to engine X alpine. Then kube control dash n lr wait the for flag set to condition Ready pod slash plain the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then kube control dash n lr get pod plain dash o json path dot spec dot containers zero dot resources echo. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 10.5: limitrange defaults, Solution, continued
2.text: Lab ten point five: limitrange defaults, Solution, continued. Run kube control dash n lr apply dash f - Y echo rejected as expected. Then api Version version one. Then kind Pod. Then metadata name toobig. Then spec. Then containers. Then - name main. Then image engine X alpine. Then resources. The remaining lines are on the screen.

2.title: Lab 10.6: qos classes
2.text: Lab ten point six: qos classes. This task is worth five points, and you should plan about five minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. In the namespace res, three Pods exist: q one, q two and q three. Write one line per Pod to about slash answers slash qos dot txt in the form pod Qo S class, sorted by Pod name, using the class that Kubernetes assigned (read it from the cluster). Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 10.6: qos classes, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run for p in q one q two q three do echo p kube control dash n res get pod p dash o json path dot status dot qos Class done sort about slash answers, and so on. Then cat about slash answers slash qos dot txt. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Recall Check 1
2.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Who uses the resource request, and who enforces the limit? Answer: The scheduler uses requests to place Pods; the kubelet and runtime enforce limits. Question two. What happens when a container exceeds its C P U limit? Its memory limit? Answer: C P U: it is throttled. Memory: it is killed ( O O M killed ) and restarted. Question three. What are the three Qo S classes? Answer: Guaranteed, Burstable and Best Effort.

2.title: Recall Check 2
2.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. When is a Pod Guaranteed? Answer: When every container has C P U and memory requests equal to its limits. Question five. What does a Resource Quota limit? Answer: The total resources and object counts of a namespace. Question six. Why can a Deployment show two slash four Pods when the namespace has a full quota? Answer: The Replica Set cannot create more Pods: exceeded quota.

2.title: Recall Check 3
2.text: Recall check three. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question seven. What does a Limit Range do? Answer: It sets default requests and limits and enforces min and max for containers in a namespace. Question eight. What is the difference between one hundred twenty-eight mebibytes and one hundred twenty-eight megabytes? Answer: Mi is one thousand twenty-four-based (mebibytes), M is one thousand-based (megabytes).

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. Request: scheduling input; Pending if no node fits. Limit: C P U throttled, memory O O M killed (one hundred thirty-seven). Units: one hundred millicores C P U, sixty-four mebibytes memory. Qo S: Guaranteed (requests equals limits), Burstable, Best Effort. Resource Quota: namespace totals and counts; describe quota. Limit Range: defaults, min, max per container; applied at creation. Commands: set resources (Deployments), yamel resources (Pods), create quota the hard flag. Quota effects: Pods must declare resources; full quota blocks the Replica Set.
